title: weight-loading-optimization
summary: Optimize the serving-level weight load path from storage to device: judge the load path on four dimensions (source, format, placement, duplication), account startup fixed overhead separately from per-request cost with bytes-and-counts lines and hit-criteria warmup validation, verify sharded weight downloads against the safetensors index, apply device-side weight prefetch only on profiled memory-bound hot spots, and order CPU-tier offload candidates by change surface. Includes source-scoped disk-loading modes, pinned staging, synchronous checkpoint save semantics and fastsafetensors broadcast/scatter/coalesced delivery. Use when startup/loading latency dominates; route DCP asynchronous save performance and distributed recovery validity to their separate skills.

applicability.scope: Diagnosing the serving-level weight load path from storage to device and choosing changes to it when startup or loading latency dominates: locating the cost by source, format, placement and duplication, accounting once-per-process loading and warmup apart from per-request cost, verifying sharded downloads, restricting device-side prefetch to profiled memory-bound hot spots and ordering CPU-tier offload; also covers source-scoped disk-loading modes, pinned staging, synchronous checkpoint save semantics, fastsafetensors broadcast/scatter/coalesced delivery and the separation of model preparation from serving. Request-time host overhead belongs to host-overhead-profiling, DCP asynchronous save performance to dcp-async-save-performance and distributed recovery validity to checkpoint-recovery-consistency
applicability.prerequisites: Flag names and API entry paths are re-verified against the pinned source revisions, and torch_npu.npu_prefetch details against the target CANN version, before they are relied on; card state is checked before launch and process placement fixed before measuring, through ascend-device-health and os-process-placement; the Diffusers enable_model_cpu_offload path requires accelerate
applicability.input_contract: The current load path's byte source, file format, host-first or direct device placement and duplicated copies across processes or instances; startup timings for loading and warmup with byte and access counts per segment, and the expected warmup hit criteria; the safetensors index weight_map and the downloaded shard set; a profile showing memory-bound hot spots and the adjacent compute or communication segments; free device memory and whether an OOM occurs during construction or inference; for cross-rank delivery, the file-to-loader-group-rank map, tensor names, shapes, dtypes and call order, the required replicated or sliced output, the model's expected shard layout and the collective backend
applicability.produced_artifact: The located load-path cost on the four dimensions with its matching lever, a startup ledger that keeps fixed overhead apart from per-request cost, a structural shard-completeness result naming the missing shards, a prefetch proposal behind an enable_prefetch switch defaulting to False or a recorded decision not to prefetch, an offload candidate order, the recorded loading mode, a distributed delivery choice with its proposed verification, and a preparation/serving record of serialized and rebuilt state, live resource owners and ABI/prepared-contract versions; proposed changes and verification targets, not a measured startup or delivery gain
failure_modes: Loading and warmup are amortized into per-request latency, or a host segment without timing points is treated as costing nothing
Warmup is accepted on total time while mismatched warmup shapes have warmed a different set of cache entries
In-flight .incomplete shards are re-downloaded as corrupt, or gap-free shard numbering is accepted without matching the index weight_map
Prefetch is forced without a profiled memory-bound hot spot or a non-memory-bound dependency window
Resolution or CFG tier-downs are applied to a construction-phase OOM, or offload is adopted when compute already hides the transfer
A free-memory probe runs on an mmap-backed load, or a run whose first mlock failure latched with only a warning is treated as fully resident
Disk counters that include cache and pipes are read as physical writes, or a run without a page-cache drop is reported as a cold start
The ceil-block scatter partition is used without checking it against the model's expected shard layout, or ranks run different orders or plans so their collectives mismatch
A faster H2D copy, local clone or rank-local filtered read is counted as a cross-rank communication gain
applicability.refusal_point: Withholds a load-path win until the verification checklist holds and keeps the distributed-delivery checks as verification targets rather than results; does not force prefetch without a safe dependency window and disables it when neither a smaller size nor a moved position removes a regression; records unsupported save behaviors as unknown; rejects mismatched execution ABI or prepared-contract versions instead of editing their tags; and implies no Ascend support from the llama.cpp or fastsafetensors mechanisms
applicability.hardware: NPU for the device-side prefetch API (torch_npu.npu_prefetch, checked against the target CANN version) and the Diffusers offload playbook; the prefetch and fastsafetensors methodology transfers while the fastsafetensors and llama.cpp APIs do not, and cross-rank completion follows each collective backend's own wait contract

recommendations: Report preparation/startup/readiness, warmups and measured work as separate numbers, with load latency split into init, header, io and get phases, the cold-cache protocol stated and the effective loading mode identical across compared runs.

Place each prefetch behind an enable_prefetch switch defaulting to False, start max_size at 50% of the theoretical size, verify a single operator first and step up to 0.7 and then 1.0 only after verified wins.

Try offload candidates in order of change surface: batch size, resolution, CFG/feature flags, CPU or layered offload, tensor-parallel degree, then activation checkpointing; re-estimate the un-overlapped transfer share after adopting each tier.
Record whole-set atomic publication, asynchronous checkpointing, multi-rank save coordination and crash durability as unknown for the fastsafetensors saver instead of assuming them.

Before adopting coalesced delivery, compare it disabled and enabled with identical checkpoint, rank mapping, backend, topology, dtype, cache state, chunk/queue budgets and consumer retention, then measure complete startup under the same accounting protocol.
limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
